name: Chromesong — Competitive Aug Aesthetic Circuit
description: Chromesong is a competitive subculture built around the aesthetic display and functional performance of cyberware augmentation — part bodybuilding competition, part fashion show, part gladiatorial arena. Competitors called 'Singers' walk the Chromesong Floor in monthly events held in repurposed industrial spaces along the Chicago Lakefront Reclamation Zone, where judges score on Integration (how seamlessly chrome meets flesh), Expression (thematic coherence of aug choices), and Live Function (real-time demonstration of aug capabilities). The scene has a fierce internal class divide between 'Born Chrome' — those who augmented young for medical necessity — and 'Buy-In Singers' who augmented purely for aesthetics.
cultural_impact: Chromesong events draw Tier 3 and 4 spectators slumming for authentic edge, pumping Φ into Shelf-adjacent economies while simultaneously threatening to gentrify the spaces that birthed the scene.
story_hooks: A Chromesong champion is offered a corporate sponsorship that would require her to use only their aug brand — and the contract has a clause about 'proprietary modifications' that sounds like ownership of her body.
A Born Chrome competitor is being systematically disqualified by judges bribed by a Buy-In aug manufacturer who wants their paid Singers to win for promotional value.
An underground Chromesong bracket called the Raw Floor has no rules and no judges — just two Singers, a crowd, and augmentations pushed past safe limits.
